name: subliminal-pulse-bed
idea: A near-subliminal electronic pulse bed, the way modern hospital procedurals hide tension under the room sound. The lead performer is an analogue synth sequencer: a dry sub-bass heartbeat pulse at a fixed 124 BPM, ticking hi-hat-like clicks high up, and nothing at all in the middle where the shouting voices sit. Ask for it as a short, genre-first tag list of about 25 words with the BPM as a number (e.g. starting 'minimal dark electronic underscore'), and keep the description flat and functional, not emotional. It barely changes until the red light, where the pulse drops to half-time for the politician's car, then it cuts dead to silence on a single choked low hit with no reverb tail and no fade. Exclude vocals, choir, humming, piano, melody.

name: shepard-rise-ticking
idea: An endless-rise illusion: stacked low strings and synth layered an octave apart that seem to climb for ever without resolving, over a ticking-clock pulse made from a mechanical watch tick. The lead performer is a low string section playing long sustained glissandi, with the tick as the only rhythm. Ask in plain-language sentences that describe the shape in seconds (a rising pressure from the first second, the climb stalling and holding a strained unison while the car crosses, a sudden cut to total silence just after ten seconds) rather than in tags. Name the illusion by what it does ('a pitch that keeps rising but never arrives'), not by a composer's name. Exclude vocals, choir, drums, kick, fade-out.

name: viola-tremolo-dread
idea: A small, rough chamber string group, led by violas and cellos, played close-miked and dry so you hear the bow and the air: fast trembling tremolo near the bridge, scraping, and slow pitch-bending slides that sour the harmony. No percussion and no electronics; the urgency comes from the bowing speed alone, swelling hard under the ambulance and thinning to one sliding viola note when the politician's car appears. Ask for it by playing technique and recording texture (sul ponticello tremolo, glissando, rosin noise, unpolished) with the genre first as 'avant-garde string chamber score'. It ends on a sharp, unison bow-stop, cutting the sound off, not decaying. Exclude vocals, choir, humming, synth, drums, piano.

name: uk-procedural-piano-motor
idea: A British police-and-hospital TV drama sound: an orchestral and electronic hybrid driven by a racing, circling high piano ostinato in an uneven 5/4 meter, over tight electronic percussion and shimmering high strings. The lead performer is the piano, kept in its upper register so it stays above the voices, with low synth bass underneath and the middle left empty. Ask for it with the 'lift' arc spelled out in words (driving from the first bar, a gear-change down at the red light into a held, glassy string chord under the politician, then a hard cold stop with all instruments dropping at once) and a number BPM around 140. Exclude vocals, choir, humming, guitar, saxophone, fade-out.

name: percussion-only-ensemble
idea: A percussion ensemble with no melody at all: big floor toms and frame drums played by hand, metal scrapes, a bowed cymbal, and one low drone note for pitch. The lead performers are three drummers locked in an urgent 150 BPM pattern that sounds like a body being worked on, accenting off the beat so it never settles. Ask for it as a genre-first tag list ('cinematic tribal percussion score, no melody') plus one sentence about dynamics: thunderous in the ambulance, suddenly reduced to a single quiet rim tick at the red light and the politician's car, then a cold end with the drone cutting off mid-note. Exclude vocals, chanting, choir, humming, strings, piano, synth lead.

name: broken-cardiac-electronica
idea: Glitchy industrial electronica built from a malfunctioning machine: a distorted kick drum standing in for an irregular heartbeat that stumbles and skips, modular synth bleeps and buzzing, granular stutter edits. The lead performer is a drum machine and modular synth rig, played harsh and dry with heavy low end and sharp highs, leaving the vocal mids clear. Ask for it as the 'collapse' arc (frantic and erratic, then the pulse slows and loses its grip under the politician's car, then a tape-stop that drags everything down to dead silence around ten seconds), described in one scene sentence after a short tag list. Exclude vocals, vocal chops, choir, humming, melodic lead, fade-out, reverb tail.
